name: Apollinarius
bio: Apollinarius is one of the named epigrammatists whose short poems are preserved in the Greek Anthology. Paton's Index of Authors dates the poet to the 4th century AD (?).
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the fourth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XI: 399, 421.

poems.title: Book XI, 399
poems.author: Apollinarius
poems.text: A grammarian riding on a donkey fell off it, and, they say, lost his memory of grammar; then afterwards he led an ordinary life without any profession, not knowing a word of what he had always been teaching. But just the opposite happened to Glycon; for, having been ignorant of the vulgar tongue, not to speak of grammar, now, by riding on Libyan donkeys and often falling off them, he has suddenly become a grammarian.

poems.title: Book XI, 421
poems.author: Apollinarius
poems.text: If you speak ill of me in my absence you do me no injury; but if you speak well of me in my presence, know that you are speaking ill of me.
